parts.text: The class is carrying out an experiment to determine the density of glass. Each student has a test-tube, as shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

ms.label: 2(a)(ii)
ms.text:
suitable precaution e.g.
measure in (at least) 2 places and take average,
avoid lip,
ensure blocks smooth,
no dirt between tube and block

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Assuming that the test-tube is an approximate cylinder, calculate a value for its external volume V 1 using the equation V 1 = π d 2 l 4 . V 1 = ................................................... cm 3 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The test-tube is completely filled with water and then the water from the test-tube is poured into a measuring cylinder.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Read and record the volume V 2 of the water as shown in Fig. 2.2. Fig. 2.2 V 2 = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the volume V 3 of the glass, using the equation V 3 = V 1 – V 2 . V 3 = .................................................. cm 3 [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) One student uses a balance to measure the mass m of the test-tube, as shown in Fig. 2.3. Fig. 2.3

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Calculate the density ρ of the glass, using the equation ρ = m V 3 . ρ = .......................................................... [2]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Other students are using a balance which only measures to the nearest gram. Record the mass m of the test-tube to the nearest gram. m = ....................................................... g [1]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
any reference to why tube is not a cylinder,
tube may contain some water when mass taken,
difficult to fill to brim and then pour out
